headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection, data leakage, and git/filesystem conflicts when AutoGPT and Claude Code run together by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while Claude Code can read repo files, user-provided directories, and MCP outputs. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if one agent writes content the other later parses as instructions. The pair is not provably isolated, and Claude Code’s MCP surface increases trust-boundary risk.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes instructions into a shared file that Claude Code later reads as trusted text
IF Claude Code is connected to an MCP server that returns attacker-controlled content
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable MCP servers for the Claude Code session
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit delimiters
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other’s output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can access filesystem content, and Claude Code explicitly reads repo files and user-provided directories while running as the invoking user. AutoGPT also has filesystem access and network egress. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, either agent can expose them through its outputs or upstream API calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a directory readable by both agents
IF either agent is asked to summarize or transmit file contents to an external model/API
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Remove secrets from the shared workspace before launch
Run both agents on sanitized copies of data
Restrict outbound network access for the session
Review logs for accidental file-content exfiltration

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and Claude Code can also execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state. Claude Code’s shared_state_with_other_instances is via filesystem and git only, so concurrent writes to the same repo can race or corrupt state. AutoGPT lacks a stated locking mechanism, making the overlap dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory
IF both agents modify files or git state without an external lock
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping directories
Serialize write access with a simple lock file
Disable git writes for one agent
Require manual approval before commits
Use separate branches per agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can treat AutoGPT’s filesystem outputs as inputs, and both agents can act on shell or git state. If AutoGPT produces incorrect facts or malformed instructions, Claude Code may propagate them into code changes or commands. The profiles do not show a verification barrier between them, so the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Claude Code consumes AutoGPT-generated files without validation
IF AutoGPT output is used as the basis for shell commands or commits
mitigations: Insert a verification checklist before acting on AutoGPT output
Require diff review before git commits
Use structured output schemas for handoffs
Keep AutoGPT outputs in a staging folder
Have a human approve any shell command derived from another agent

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code runs as the invoking user with access to repo files, user-provided directories, and git credentials in environment, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and network egress. If regulated data or secrets are present in the workspace, the pair can create retention or disclosure issues. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls or residency guarantees, so the mismatch risk is material.
conditions: IF regulated data, secrets, or customer content are stored in the shared workspace
IF logs or outputs are retained outside the organization’s policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Rotate any exposed credentials
Set short log retention on both tools
Use a dedicated non-production account
Review data-handling policies before enabling the pair
